name: Stokely Carmichael (Kwame Ture)
role: Civil rights leader; SNCC chairman (1966-67); Black Panther Party honorary prime minister; later Pan-Africanist organiser in Guinea (as Kwame Ture)
summary: Stokely Carmichael led SNCC and popularised "Black Power" in 1966, calling for black-run political and economic institutions and refusing the Vietnam draft. After moving to Guinea in 1969 he took the name Kwame Ture and became a Nkrumaist: a Pan-Africanist and scientific socialist who held that capitalism must be destroyed, that Israel and America are settler colonies, and that revolution may require killing.

public-ownership.rationale: Defined scientific socialism as a system where the means of production are owned and controlled by the masses and the profits divided equally among them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called private property the cornerstone of a "stupid" capitalist society and held up traditional African communal society, where land belonged to the community, as the model for the modern age.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Said capitalism must be smashed and that "revolution overturns and destroys everything that gets in its path", and in 1996 said unity "can only be achieved by revolution, by destroying capitalism".

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Told the Whittier audience they must be "willing to kill" to bring about their system and must understand the necessity to kill; in 1967 he called armed struggle the only road; in 1996 he said "if we have to shed blood to advance humanity, no problem".

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Said that America's land belongs to the red man and that the settlers wiped out a nation to take it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Said workers are forced to sell their labor and the capitalist who owns the means of production takes the profit, citing Ali and Frazier getting $800,000 while the promoter takes $30 million.

conscription.rationale: Told the Berkeley crowd that the only power black people have is to say "Hell no!" to the draft, and in 1966 wrote that black people "won't fight to save the present society, in Vietnam or anywhere else".

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Israel is a European settler colony where European Jews took over Palestine, changed its name and oppressed the original Palestinian Arab owners.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Called South Africa, Rhodesia, Australia, Israel, America and Canada European settler colonies that took the land of their original owners by force.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: Said the revolution is about land and that people must be willing to kill to bring about their system.

land-redistribution.rationale: Pointed out that in Lowndes County eighty-six white families own 90 percent of the land and said "there must be reallocation of land, of money."

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Rejected assimilation and wanted the black community developed with "its own cultural identity, life patterns, and institutions" inside the larger society.

defeat-communism.rationale: Stood with Marxism-Leninism, praised Vietnam and China against America, and said America must be destroyed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said capitalism must be destroyed and put forward Marxism-Leninism and scientific socialism as the system to replace it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Wrote that with power "the masses could make or participate in making the decisions which govern their destinies", and that the poor must control the anti-poverty programs and funds that affect them.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Reaffirmed on behalf of SNCC the right of black people to defend themselves.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Argued that black people must organise their own political base and power, and asked whites to organise inside white communities rather than inside the black movement.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Said America must be destroyed and that Africans must pose a system diametrically opposed to capitalism, to be fought into place by revolution.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Described institutional racism as the force that keeps black communities poor and colonised and as the problem black liberation must overcome.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Told the Berkeley crowd there is a higher law than the laws of McNamara, Rusk and Johnson, "the law of each of us".

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Condemned the settler seizure of land and genocide of the original owners as barbaric.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: Wrote that black money should go "into the communal pocket", that black people must control the poverty money they spend, and that the cooperative concept should be applied in business and banking; in 1971 he said Black Power is the black man in control of black land.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Said the Vietnamese and the Palestinians will win because theirs is a just struggle, and said America is being beaten in Vietnam.

notes: Rests on his speeches, essays and a 1967 interview. Positions changed: in 1966-67 he led a black-power movement for black-run institutions; from 1969 he was a Nkrumaist Pan-Africanist and scientific socialist, so the Whittier 1971 speech (s5) outranks the earlier ones where they differ. Searched: Project Gutenberg, the local news and Congress corpora (nothing by him); Voteview does not apply. Themes searched in his own words: war and draft, violence, capitalism and socialism, land, settler states, Israel, race and organisation, law and protest. Nothing found on gender, religion, the family, immigration, the environment, or the design of government institutions, so those are null.
